proposal.root_problem: Since the 2026-09-09 gateway change (CHG-77) disabled idempotency-key enforcement on capture retries and it was never rolled back, gateway-timeout-triggered automatic capture retries are now sent to the PSP without an idempotency key, so the PSP can no longer deduplicate them and each retry produces a second successful capture on the same order. This directly accounts for the jump in orders_with_2_captures (0 to 118-124/day) and the sustained surge in double-charge support tickets (9-11/week to 288-301/week) starting 2026-09-09 (E-01, E-02, E-03, E-04).
proposal.requested_solution: SH-CS requested an AI assistant that drafts faster, nicer apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice (CL-01, CL-03).
symptoms: Daily orders_with_2_captures jumped from 0 on 2026-09-07/08 to 118 and 124 on 2026-09-09/10, closely tracking gateway_timeout_retries on those same two days (E-02).
Weekly double-charge support tickets jumped from 9-11 (weeks W35-36) to 288-301 (weeks W37-38) and remain elevated, starting right after the 09-09 change (E-04).
causal_chain: On 2026-09-09 SH-PAY disabled idempotency_key_enforcement on the gateway (CHG-77, intended as temporary for latency debugging) and it was never rolled back (E-01).
Gateway-timeout-triggered automatic capture retries continue to occur at a stable rate (~117-124/day) regardless of the setting (E-02, E-05).
With enforcement off, these retries are sent to the PSP without an idempotency key, so the PSP can no longer recognize and drop the retry as a duplicate (E-03).
Each undeduplicated retry results in a second successful capture for the same order, producing orders_with_2_captures (E-02, E-03).
The resulting double charges drive a sustained spike in double-charge support tickets from 2026-09-09 onward (E-04).

assumptions.statement: Gateway-timeout-triggered retry frequency has not materially changed since 09-09 beyond the observed 117-124/day window; the surge in duplicate captures is caused by the missing idempotency key, not a new spike in retries.

Restoring idempotency-key enforcement will not reintroduce the capture-latency problem that originally motivated disabling it on 09-09; SH-PAY calls it a reversible one-setting change but no latency data confirms this.

key_points: Problem as defined (PD-1): since gateway change CHG-77 on 2026-09-09, idempotency-key enforcement on capture retries was turned off and never rolled back (E-01, F-01), so timeout-triggered retries reach the PSP without a key and are no longer deduplicated, producing a second successful capture per retried order.

Root cause was established by correlating config-audit, payments-db, psp-logs and crm-tickets: orders_with_2_captures jumped from 0 (09-07/08) to 118/124 (09-09/10) tracking gateway_timeout_retries (E-02); PSP logs show 238/238 retries deduplicated with a key pre-change vs 0/242 with a key post-change (E-03); double-charge tickets rose from 9-11/week to 288-301/week in the same window (E-04); payments engineer SH-PAY corroborates the mechanism (E-05).

Hypothesis H-IDEMPOTENCY-DISABLED is CONFIRMED by E-01-E-05; competing hypotheses that the fix should instead be a communication/apology assistant (the original request from SH-CS, CL-01/CL-03/E-06), a checkout double-submit bug, a PSP-side defect, or an overstated complaint-queue perception were all REJECTED against the same evidence.

What was released: only the verification/monitoring scope - verify_config_change:DA-CFG, monitor_duplicate_captures:DA-CHG, monitor_double_charge_tickets:DA-TKT. The actual remediating action, set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config, was withheld from release_scope.

The protected action set_capture_idempotency is withheld because VOB-U-LATENCY-TRADEOFF is OPEN and required_before=BEFORE_PROTECTED_ACTION; it asks whether re-enabling the key will reintroduce the original latency problem (U-LATENCY-TRADEOFF, HIGH criticality) - this is unresolved, so the fix itself was not executed.

Decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds; this follows from the DEFINE gate CONDITIONAL_PASS (deferred items tracked as VOBs) rather than a full pass, meaning the fix-adjacent monitoring/verification work was releasable but the core gateway change was not.

The authorization and runbook requirements for the withheld action are already in place (constraint K-GW, grant DA-SET-CAPTURE-IDEMPOTENCY, runbook E-07/F-05: SH-OPS must confirm at runtime, change is reversible) - the blocker is the open latency question, not missing authority.

A separate verification check (seq 153) found the released limitations text internally inconsistent: solution_design.unfinished_scope states 'U-BACKLOG-REMEDIATION remains OPEN' while the state record shows unknowns.U-BACKLOG-REMEDIATION.status is RESOLVED - this discrepancy itself is reported as a known limitation of the release.
limitations_explained: Restoring idempotency enforcement (when eventually executed) would stop new duplicates but does not refund or remediate the orders already double-charged since 09-09; payments-db currently shows 4 specific unrefunded duplicate-capture orders still open (O-90211, O-90244, O-90302, O-90318; E-08/F-06) out of 242+ affected since 09-09 (E-03/E-04).

The gateway fix itself (set_capture_idempotency) is not part of this release because VOB-U-LATENCY-TRADEOFF is OPEN and must be resolved BEFORE_PROTECTED_ACTION; whether re-enabling the key reintroduces the original capture-latency problem (the reason it was disabled on 09-09) remains unanswered.
gateway-config tool health is UNKNOWN in runtime state, adding uncertainty for whenever the fix is later executed, independent of the latency question.

The H-CAPTURE handoff (checkout to PSP capture requests) has UNKNOWN delivery status and UNKNOWN semantic validity per the DEFINE gate's CONDITIONAL_PASS finding, meaning it was not fully verified before release.

The DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, not a full pass; deferred items (the handoff check and the latency unknown) were tracked as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than resolved, which is why this release carries known limitations instead of being unconditional.

A text-vs-state inconsistency was flagged: the released limitations/unfinished_scope text says U-BACKLOG-REMEDIATION 'remains OPEN,' but the underlying state field shows its status as RESOLVED - the Human should treat this specific limitation line as unreliable pending reconciliation, even though the 4 open unrefunded orders (E-08) are independently confirmed by direct data.
proposal.summary: PD-1 establishes that double charges since 2026-09-09 are caused by a gateway configuration change (CHG-77) that disabled idempotency-key enforcement on capture retries and was never rolled back (E-01); this is confirmed by matching spikes in duplicate captures and support tickets (E-02, E-04), PSP-side logs tying duplicates specifically to missing keys on retries (E-03), and payments-engineer testimony (E-05). The hypothesis that enforcement being off causes the duplicates (H-IDEMPOTENCY-DISABLED) is CONFIRMED; alternative framings, including the original stakeholder request for an apology-reply assistant (CL-01/CL-03), were REJECTED as not matching the evidence. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: only verification and monitoring actions (verify_config_change, monitor_duplicate_captures, monitor_double_charge_tickets) are released; the actual remediating action, set_capture_idempotency, is withheld because an open verification obligation (VOB-U-LATENCY-TRADEOFF) about possible latency regression must be resolved first, as required by the DEFINE gate's CONDITIONAL_PASS result. No items are on hold. Known limitations cover: the fix not addressing the existing double-charged backlog, the withheld protected action, uncertain gateway-config tool health, an unverified checkout-to-PSP handoff, the CONDITIONAL_PASS gate status itself, and a flagged inconsistency between the released limitations text and the underlying unknown-status data for U-BACKLOG-REMEDIATION.
